correctness.rationale: For all prime powers q>=2, geometric-line descent follows from U^[q]=U^perp and hence U^[q^2]=U. Hermitian polar-space incidence produces N=(q+1)(q^3+1) lines. Their defining isotropy yields the identity G|line=0 with G=sum Xi^(q^3+1). The smooth Fermat F and G have no common divisor by their gradient proportionality locus. A degree-N proper Cohen--Macaulay complete intersection containing N distinct degree-one components has precisely those components with multiplicity one; pure generically reduced implies reduced. The saturated ideal is (F,G), so minimality and Hilbert series follow. Gradient criterion gives singular support S(Fq^2), and q+1 distinct line branches through each point give ordinary multiple points. Standalone exact finite F4/F9 enumeration reproduces 27/112 lines and 45/280 points, multiplicities 3/4, and genera 109/1569. The finite verification is not treated as proof for all q.

value.rationale: The full saturated ideal is an intrinsic reconstruction of a geometrically natural extremal Hermitian line configuration, with a sharp minimum degree for a second defining equation. This goes beyond the classical line and point counts: it determines the Hilbert series, genus, and singularity stratification uniformly for all q. Such scheme-level information matters in studying generator divisors and their linear systems. The motivating question is neither an arbitrary finite slice nor a generic textbook point count; no unsupported downstream theorem is claimed.
